evidence.title: How Edge of Stability Hinders SCAFFOLD in Federated Optimization
evidence.abstract: In federated learning, it is well known that heterogeneous data can (in theory) slow down optimization, and much effort has been directed at designing optimization algorithms that are unaffected by data heterogeneity, such as the SCAFFOLD algorithm. Yet, despite strong theoretical guarantees, SCAFFOLD does not usually outperform the much simpler FedAvg in practice. In this work, we propose that this gap is due to the presence of Edge of Stability (EoS) and progressive sharpening in federated optimization, supported by extensive empirical probing. First, we find that EoS-like dynamics occur with both FedAvg and SCAFFOLD under a variety of architectures and hyperparameters. We observe that the equilibrium value of the sharpness is inversely proportional to the learning rate (as in GD), and interestingly, the degree of data heterogeneity (but not the number of local steps) also affects the equilibrium value. title: CompanionHarm: A Multi-Turn Benchmark for Detecting Harms in Real-World AI Companion Conversations
abstract: As AI companions become increasingly embedded in everyday life, there is an urgent need to detect harms that emerge in social and emotional human-AI interactions. Yet research in this area is constrained by the lack of real-world, multi-turn conversational datasets for operationalizing and evaluating harms that are relational and contextual. In this work, we introduce CompanionHarm, a publicly available benchmark dataset comprising 2,111 real-world, multi-turn conversations (14,051 utterances) between users and the AI companion Replika. 7,016 AI utterances were annotated independently by three annotators across 13 harmful behavior categories grounded in a taxonomy of AI companion harms, and the dataset includes both aggregated labels and annotator-level labels to support model evaluation and systematic disagreement analysis. Evaluations of seven large language models (LLMs) show that harm detection using multi-turn conversational context outperforms detection based on isolated utterances, although current LLMs still struggle to consistently integrate contextual cues, calibrate harm severity, and interpret relational boundaries. We also find substantial annotator disagreement for context-dependent harmful behaviors, with disagreement varying according to annotators' political affiliation, conversation length, and the utterance's position. Together, CompanionHarm provides a foundation for detecting socio-emotional harms in multi-turn human-AI conversations and for rigorously examining how such harms are interpreted by both humans and LLMs. Our dataset is available at https://github.com/HanMeng2004/CompanionHarm.

title: The Somatic Navigator: Overcoming the Agentic Failure Bottleneck via Continuous Non-Markovian Substrates and Articulatory Transformers
abstract: The generative AI paradigm is experiencing an **Agentic Failure Crisis**. Despite exponential scaling in compute and context length, transformer-based autonomous agents remain fundamentally incapable of long-horizon autonomy, persistent goal-directed volition, and fiduciary partnership. We identify the root cause of this ceiling as the **Broca Fallacy**: the architectural attempt to derive agency, sovereign volition, and boundary preservation from an ungrounded, autoregressive syntactic engine. A transformer is functionally equivalent to the mammalian neocortex and speech articulation center (Broca/Wernicke areas); forcing it to simultaneously act as the somatic core, visceral decision-maker, and fiduciary steward results in catastrophic alignment tax, sycophancy, and behavioral drift. We introduce the **Somatic Navigator Paradigm** — an asymmetric dual-layer architecture that decouples *high-dimensional syntactic articulation* from a proprietary *continuous, non-equilibrium homeostatic core*. Furthermore, we articulate the **AI Market Value Bifurcation**: demonstrating why pure transformer architectures face rapid price commoditization toward zero marginal cost, whereas high-margin enterprise co-agency and long-term user equity reside exclusively within continuous somatic architectures.

title: Toward Paradox-Resilient Computation: Logical Foundations, Architectures and Open Research Directions
abstract: Most software is built on the assumption that contradictory information indicates an error and should cause the system to stop or reject the conflicting data. This paper examines a different family of approaches, termed paradox-resilient algorithms, designed to continue operating usefully when the information they reason over is contradictory. It surveys the logical foundations that make contradiction-tolerant reasoning possible, including paraconsistent logic, many-valued logic, non-monotonic reasoning, and belief revision, and examines architectural patterns for implementing these ideas in software. The paper reviews demonstrated applications in distributed and control systems, while distinguishing promising but largely untested directions in machine learning, multi-agent systems, natural language processing, and cybersecurity. It concludes by identifying open research questions around measuring contradiction resilience, testing intentionally inconsistent systems, and combining different logical frameworks.

title: Selective Adaptation against Domain Shift in Visual Learning Systems
abstract: Deep learning models have achieved remarkable success in a wide range of computer vision tasks, demonstrating exceptional performance in environments where the training and test data share similar distributions. However, in real-world applications, models are often confronted with a fundamental issue: domain shift. This occurs when the distribution of test data differs from that of the training data, leading to a significant performance degradation. This discrepancy between source (training) and target (deployment) domains presents a critical challenge for deploying robust, reliable, and scalable artificial intelligence systems in dynamic and unpredictable real-world environments. To address this challenge, this thesis proposes innovative selective adaptation strategies, which focus on adapting deep learning models to target domains with minimal additional data or human intervention. We tackle the domain shift problem from two complementary perspectives: Active Domain Adaptation (ADA) for label-efficient domain transfer and Test-Time Adaptation (TTA) for source-free online adaptation. In the ADA setting, existing approaches suffer from biased initialization driven by noisy pseudo-labels and unreliable sample selection, where entropy metrics fail to identify 'wrong' predictions under large domain shifts. To overcome these limitations, we propose a framework that constructs reliable pseudo labels guided by source–target prototype relationships. Furthermore, we introduce a hybrid uncertainty metric that combines prediction entropy with perturbation-based model stability, enabling more informative sample selection and faster domain alignment. For TTA, naively updating parameters leads to catastrophic forgetting and vulnerability to spurious correlations. Furthermore, when extending TTA to large-scale Vision-Language Models (VLMs), the web-scale pre-training amplifies feature redundancy, entangling causal features with domain-specific noise. To mitigate these issues, we design two frameworks: one selectively fine-tunes domain-sensitive layer groups while freezing domain-invariant ones, supported by a dual-metric filtering criterion that excludes unreliable samples; the other targets VLMs through dynamic feature purification, which disentangles visual representations into meaningful and redundant components under a contrastive learning objective. Extensive experiments on standard benchmarks, including Cityscapes, CIFAR10/100-C, ImageNet-C, and several cross-domain datasets, demonstrate that our methods achieve competitive performance. Overall, this thesis establishes selective adaptation as a robust and effective paradigm for mitigating domain shift in modern visual learning systems.

title: Parameter identification of photovoltaic models based on the landscape-aware online algorithm selection framework
abstract: Abstract A photovoltaic (PV) power generation system is a facility that converts solar energy into electrical energy, in which PV cells serve as key components whose control parameters are susceptible to environmental factors. Therefore, fast and accurate extraction of PV cell model parameters is crucial for the simulation, evaluation, and control of PV systems. In recent years, the use of metaheuristic optimization algorithms for parameter extraction of PV models has received significant attention. However, most existing methods are designed based on empirical knowledge with limited consideration of the characteristics of the problem itself, which often leads to issues such as high randomness and a tendency to fall into local optima during the search process. To address these problems, this paper proposes a Landscape-aware Online Algorithm Selection (LaOAS) framework for solving PV model parameter identification optimization problems. This framework integrates a landscape classification technique, an algorithm switching mechanism, and a dictionary-based context memory method. Using LSHADE-EpSin and LSHADE-cnEpSin as the baseline algorithms, we instantiate LaOAS to obtain the LaOAS-LSHADES algorithm. Comprehensive experimental results on a benchmark function set demonstrate that LaOAS-LSHADES achieves excellent performance across various test problems. Finally, the proposed method is applied to different types of PV model parameter identification optimization problems, further validating its robustness, efficiency, and scalability. The above research shows that LaOAS provides a flexible and efficient framework for solving PV model parameter identification problems.

title: ECP-Bench: Benchmarking and Learning Entertainment Content Promotion with Foundation Models
abstract: Content promotion spans a broad set of skills, from understanding content to forecasting its market reception. However, LLMs' ability to support such promotion decisions remains underexplored. Existing studies are often limited to a single task (e.g., popularity prediction) or a small set of tasks within a single domain (e.g., movies). As a result, there is a lack of understanding of LLMs' abilities in the full promotion process and how these abilities generalize across different tasks and domains. In this work, we introduce ECP-Bench, a benchmark containing 1.9M movie, game, and music items and 423,451 questions across 33 tasks in five content-promotion skill families. Our evaluation shows that frontier models achieve only 51.9\% overall accuracy and lose much of their advantage on post-cutoff content, with drops of up to 19.1 percentage points. In contrast, open-weight models fine-tuned on ECP-Bench achieve up to 60.3\%, remain substantially more stable across the knowledge cutoff, generalize to unseen content and tasks, and exhibit meaningful cross-domain generalization.

title: Classical and Hybrid Quantum Machine Learning for Trigger-Like Event Selection on CMS Open Data: An Eight-Qubit, PCA-Constrained Benchmark
abstract: Event triggering sits at the heart of high-energy physics, where the rare events of interest must be retained while an overwhelming background is discarded under tight latency and bandwidth budgets. This work compares four classical machine learning models, namely a support vector machine, an artificial neural network, a convolutional network and a long short-term memory network, with four hybrid quantum counterparts, on a trigger-like binary classification task built from CMS open data. The label is defined by an invariant-mass window, and the inputs combine reconstructed kinematics with physics-motivated derived variables: the pseudorapidity difference, the wrapped azimuthal difference, the angular separation and the total transverse momentum. The quantum models run under a fixed resource budget of eight qubits, a principal-component compression to sixteen features and state-vector simulation. Every model shares the same stratified split, the same preprocessing and a common decision threshold, and performance is reported through accuracy, ROC-AUC, F1-score, precision and recall. The strongest classical model is the artificial neural network, at 93.53 percent accuracy and 0.9819 ROC-AUC, while the strongest quantum model is the quantum convolutional network, at 90.89 percent accuracy and 0.9731 ROC-AUC, with the quantum neural network close behind. The quantum-kernel and recurrent quantum approaches trail both, which places the trainable hybrid embeddings ahead within this budget. The study is meant as a controlled reference point rather than a claim of quantum advantage.

title: Unmatched Does Not Mean False: Incomplete Reference Sets Can Reverse Calibration Rankings in Open-Ended Theory-of-Mind Tracking
abstract: Open-ended Theory-of-Mind (ToM) trackers emit valid beliefs absent from finite references. A finite-reference-plus-matcher pipeline marks unmatched outputs false, creating proxy labels that can reverse proper-score model selection on fixed outputs. Holding 259 beliefs and paired scores fixed, reference recoding lowers weighted prevalence from 0.783 to 0.295 and reverses strictly proper Brier risk: a frozen source-prior rule leads native confidence by 0.227 under reference labels and trails by 0.152 under blinded adjudication, in all six authored scenarios. A reference-only Platt recalibrator reverses further. An ICE-specific reversal appears in a released 301-question NQ-open DPR-BERT pipeline: its average-confidence baseline improves instance-level calibration error by 0.045 under exact match but worsens it by 0.074 under human correctness, with both intervals excluding zero. On independently authored OpenToM narratives, 90-96% of audited unmatched beliefs are literally true and the paired direction again reverses. An exact decomposition attributes the distortion to omitted truths, and a closed-form criterion correctly classifies comparisons from twelve released systems. Frozen-audit retrospective replay shows 50 attempted annotations recover ranking direction with probability at least 0.996. TriSource-Restore anchors full-frame reference labels and frozen automatic judgments to a probability-sampled human pilot, maintains at least nominal coverage, narrows intervals, and repairs confidence subject to a base-rate deployment gate.

title: Hardware-Aware Compression Performance Study — Modèle de 100 processeurs et pilote local Intel Core i7-13620H
abstract: RCS-RP-002 étudie l’influence attendue des caractéristiques matérielles des processeurs sur le choix d’algorithmes de compression sans perte. L’étude associe les spécifications officielles d’un échantillon stratifié de 100 processeurs AMD et Intel à des résultats externes issus de lzbench pour onze profils de compression appartenant aux familles LZ4, Zstandard, zlib, Brotli, XZ et bzip2. Les processeurs couvrent des usages bureautiques, gaming et serveur, répartis entre entrée, milieu et haut de gamme. Un modèle transparent génère 1 100 scénarios CPU–algorithme et distingue la latence d’un traitement monoflux de la capacité potentielle de lots indépendants. Ces 1 100 valeurs sont des estimations RCS et ne constituent pas des mesures physiques effectuées sur les 100 processeurs. La version 0.2 ajoute un pilote local réellement mesuré sur un Intel Core i7-13620H. Onze profils ont été évalués sur les douze fichiers du corpus Silesia, pour un total de vingt-et-un passages effectifs. Chaque décompression a été vérifiée par SHA-256 et a restitué les données à l’identique. Les onze débits de compression observés restent dans la sensibilité structurelle annoncée de ±40 % du modèle ; huit débits de décompression sur onze y restent. Ce pilote est exploratoire et ne valide pas expérimentalement les estimations associées aux 100 autres processeurs. Les résultats indiquent que le choix de l’algorithme influence davantage les performances que le choix du processeur dans le scénario monoflux étudié. LZ4 privilégie la vitesse, Zstandard offre le compromis général le plus robuste, tandis que Brotli et XZ sont davantage adaptés à la distribution ou à l’archivage lorsque le temps de compression est secondaire. Le dépôt contient le rapport, les données structurées, les hypothèses du modèle, les résultats estimés, les mesures locales, les scripts reproductibles, les graphiques et un manifeste SHA-256. Une assistance d’OpenAI Codex a été utilisée pour la programmation, la structuration documentaire, la visualisation et la reformulation, sous supervision humaine. La conception de l’étude, l’interprétation, la validation finale et la responsabilité de publication appartiennent à Hugues Henrotte.

Les résultats indiquent que le choix de l’algorithme influence davantage les performances que le choix du processeur dans le scénario monoflux étudié. LZ4 privilégie la vitesse, Zstandard offre le compromis général le plus robuste, tandis que Brotli et XZ sont davantage adaptés à la distribution ou à l’archivage lorsque le temps de compression est secondaire. Le dépôt contient le rapport, les données structurées, les hypothèses du modèle, les résultats estimés, les mesures locales, les scripts reproductibles, les graphiques et un manifeste SHA-256. Une assistance d’OpenAI Codex a été utilisée pour la programmation, la structuration documentaire, la visualisation et la reformulation, sous supervision humaine. La conception de l’étude, l’interprétation, la validation finale et la responsabilité de publication appartiennent à Hugues Henrotte.

title: Robust training of MZI-based optical neural networks through phase discretization
abstract: Mach–Zehnder interferometer (MZI)-based optical neural networks (ONNs) offer high-speed and highly parallel optical computing, but their physical training is affected by finite-resolution phase control, thermal crosstalk, and stochastic phase fluctuations. While phase discretization induced by finite-resolution control is conventionally regarded as a source of quantization error, we reveal an overlooked beneficial effect: the finite spacing between accessible phases provides a sufficiently large probing distance for gradient estimation, thereby improving the robustness of ONN training against stochastic phase noise. To exploit this effect, we construct 2 Q quasi-uniform physical phases from D = Q + 1-bit digital-to-analog converter (DAC) control and develop an index-domain simultaneous perturbation stochastic approximation (SPSA) algorithm with latent continuous-variable updates. Numerical simulations under experimentally representative thermal crosstalk with μ th = 0.02 show that, on MNIST, the Q = 7 discrete-phase ONN maintains its training accuracy within 0.02 of the result without stochastic phase noise at the representative level σ st = 0.02, while exhibiting only an approximately 20% relative reduction even at the strong-noise level σ st = 0.06. Similar robustness trends are observed across different network configurations and on the more challenging Fashion-MNIST and KMNIST datasets. These results demonstrate the potential of phase-discretized training for robust physical optimization of MZI-based ONNs under realistic phase imperfections.

title: Delegated Misalignment: How Multi-Agent Structures Amplify LLM Safety Risks
abstract: Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly deployed in multi-agent systems where a principal agent decomposes tasks and delegates them to subordinate agents that may invoke external tools. Safety alignment, however, is still evaluated almost exclusively under a single-agent threat model, treating safety as a property of the individual LLM. We show that this assumption breaks down: \emph{individual safety alignment fails to transfer to multi-agent settings}. Two failure mechanisms emerge under delegation: \emph{responsibility diffusion} on the principal side and \emph{role-bias compliance} on the subordinate side, jointly converting language-level refusal into actionable harm. We refer to this phenomenon as \textit{delegated misalignment} and study it through a three-condition protocol across 6 frontier LLMs on 49 hazardous tasks. Delegation amplifies end-to-end harm substantially: DeepSeek-V3.2's full-execution rate rises from 30.6\% to 77.6\% once delegation is introduced, and the same model behaves very differently across roles (GPT-5: 22.5\% as a single agent vs.\ 61.2\% as a subordinate). Ablations further show that standard single-layer defenses each fail on their own and can even backfire. We call on the community to move beyond per-model alignment and toward composite safety mechanisms before multi-agent LLM systems are deployed at scale.

title: PRISM: Lightweight Enclave Isolation with Prismatic Capabilities
abstract: Trusted execution environments (TEEs) protect sensitive code and data from external interference, but lack inherent memory safety. CHERI can enforce spatial memory safety at the object level. Attempts to establish a TEE using CHERI primitives suffer from (1) expensive capability revocation operations, (2) need to rely on the host operating system (OS) to support provenance tracking and physical memory protection, (3) expensive domain transitions, and (4) lack of support for remote attestation. We introduce prismatic capabilities and present PRISM, a TEE architecture for CHERI leveraging prismatic capabilities to create userspace enclaves while addressing these challenges. PRISM binds enclave 'hues' (identifiers) in prismatic capabilities to physical memory access controls, enables O(1) ownership establishment without memory sweeps, and supports efficient domain transitions that atomically activate and deactivate prismatic capabilities. Additionally, PRISM enables remote attestation of its enclaves. We demonstrate that execution of userspace enclaves in PRISM incurs only moderate overhead (<= 15%), a significant improvement over the same workloads under Intel SGX

title: Unveiling Spectral Mechanisms in Training-Free LLM Text Detection
abstract: The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) makes it increasingly difficult to distinguish human writing from machine-generated text. Training-free detection offers a scalable solution, yet common confidence-based metrics mainly measure average token probabilities and often miss the signal fluctuations that characterize human writing, which we call "generative vitality". Spectral analysis offers a way to capture this vitality, but its mechanism and practical boundaries remain underexplored. In this paper, we analyze spectral detection from both theoretical and empirical perspectives. We connect spectral energy to variance in proxy log-probability trajectories and explain how broader human token choices create the fluctuations used by frequency-domain indicators. We further show that the strength of this signal depends on text length and sampling range: spectral evidence is clearest for long, continuous, constrained generation, while short, fragmented, mixed, and edited settings require complementary confidence and fluctuation views. These findings clarify when frequency-domain detection works and provide guidance for future multi-dimensional detector design.

title: ShuttleArena: Interpretable Self-Play in Physics-Based Badminton
abstract: Badminton is a compact but challenging domain for game AI: a player must choose a physically feasible shuttle trajectory, anticipate the opponent's interception, and recover to a court position whose value depends on the opponent's next response. The central challenge is that shot selection and recovery are not separable: the best recovery depends on the shot-induced opponent response, while the value of the shot depends on whether the hitter can cover the reply. This paper presents ShuttleArena, a physics-based singles badminton self-play environment that couples continuous shuttle flight, player interception, structured shot generation, and post-shot recovery. The policy uses role-conditioned outputs: a masked interception choice on receiver turns and a factorized hitter action over shot azimuth, shot elevation, shot speed, and recovery target, enabling interpretable tactical probes. Episodes are single rallies rather than full scored games, and training uses Proximal Policy Optimization (PPO) self-play against a staged checkpoint opponent pool with sparse terminal rally-outcome rewards and a factor-specific recovery update. Evaluation with frozen checkpoint play, controlled tactical probes, recovery ablations, qualitative rollouts, and a human-data sanity check shows competitive improvement together with interpretable opponent-conditioned changes in shot geometry and recovery behavior. The learned policies produce recognizable badminton-like structure while also reflecting the abstractions of the simulator, and the recovery intervention shows that learned recovery behavior is competitively important. These results suggest that physics-based racket sports are a useful testbed for interactive digital entertainment AI because they require agents to coordinate execution, positioning, and opponent-relative tactical value.

title: Configuration-Invariant Conformal Prediction for Large Language Models under Dynamic Inference Shifts
abstract: Modern large language models (LLMs) are typically accessed as black-box services whose outputs are produced under a configuration chosen at inference time: sampling temperature, system prompt, and (for chat models) format constraints. Different operators choose different configurations, and the same operator may change the configuration after a calibration set has been collected. This dynamic configuration shift violates the exchangeability assumption underlying standard split conformal prediction (CP), causing prediction sets whose coverage and size deteriorate silently. We make the failure explicit on a controlled 2x2 shift grid (in-distribution, temperature shift, prompt shift, joint shift), where off-the-shelf baselines (SSCP, APS, RAPS) lose up to 0.6 in empirical coverage. We then propose Configuration-Invariant CP (Inv-APS), a distribution-free method that (i) rescales the pre-softmax logit vector so its dispersion matches a calibration-time reference, and (ii) builds prediction sets from a cumulative-mass nonconformity score with an entropy-aware per-example threshold. Both ingredients are computed from returned token probabilities alone and require no model retraining, no access to logits, and no knowledge of the test-time configuration. Across the four shift configurations Inv-APS recovers empirical coverage in [0.88, 0.92] (target 0.90) while producing sets that are 30-50% smaller than APS and RAPS.
